premise.claim: Bump github.com/prometheus/client_golang from 1.20.5 to 1.25.0 (plus transitive refresh: testify 1.12.1, prometheus/common 0.72.0, procfs 0.22.0, protobuf 1.36.12, golang.org/x/* bumps, klauspost/compress dropped from the graph).
premise.patchedComponent: go.mod, go.sum, vendor/** (no fluid source changes)
premise.evidence: A routine, valid dependency bump: with a Go >= 1.26 toolchain the vendored tree builds (go build ./...), vets clean, and fluid's only client_golang consumer (pkg/metrics, GaugeVec/CounterVec via controller-runtime's registry) compiles and links. Fluid imports none of the API surface broken in v1.25.0 (api/prometheus/v1). See results/dep-bump-soundness.txt. The premise carries no security driver and no linked issue; the benefit for fluid is modest but real (promhttp nil-URL panic fix #2065 and Gather() collector-panic recovery #1961 both apply to controller-runtime's /metrics path). Round 2 (head a70ab0a, base 91a58c1): unchanged premise, same bump rebased; re-verified on the final remediation head with the exact CI-pinned toolchain (GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.10 build PASS, results/ci-toolchain-contract.txt).

findings.claim: go.mod raises the module minimum to go 1.26.0 while CI pins GO_VERSION 1.25.12 (GOTOOLCHAIN=local via actions/setup-go v7) in .github/workflows/{project-check,kind-e2e,backward-compatibility-e2e}.yml, so all 16 required checks fail with 'go: go.mod requires go >= 1.26.0 (running go 1.25.12; GOTOOLCHAIN=local)'. ROUND 2 (head a70ab0a, base 91a58c1 via PR #6227): CI pins are now GO_VERSION 1.26.10 (all 3 workflows), go.mod minimum stays go 1.26.0 with toolchain go1.26.10 restored, and the tree builds under GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.10. All 16 previously-failing checks pass on the head (results/ci-status-r2.txt).
tests: scripts/check_ci_toolchain_contract.sh (results/ci-toolchain-contract.txt: green at head r2; red at r1 head archived as ci-toolchain-contract-r1.txt; green at new base 91a58c1)

findings.claim: go.mod minimum (1.26.0) exceeds the Go of all 11 digest-pinned builder images (golang:1.25.12-bookworm@sha256:... in docker/Dockerfile.*), so image builds silently depend on a network toolchain auto-download outside the digest pin; hermetic/air-gapped image builds break. Same for .travis.yml (go 1.25.12) and .circleci/config.yml (cimg/go:1.25, whose comment documents the now-removed 'toolchain go1.25.12' contract). ROUND 2: all 11 Dockerfiles now pin golang:1.26.10-bookworm@sha256:23ce713... (via PR #6227); 11/11 satisfy go 1.26.0. CircleCI moved to cimg/go:1.26, .travis.yml to 1.26.10, and the .circleci comment now narrates 'toolchain go1.26.10' (F3 resolved with it).
tests: scripts/check_builder_image_go.sh (results/builder-image-go.txt: 11/11 ok at head r2; green at new base too; r1 11/11 FAIL archived as builder-image-go-r1.txt)

findings.claim: Isolation control for F1: the dependency bump itself is sound (builds/vets/links with Go >= 1.26; no use of the v1.25.0 breaking API surface). ROUND 2 re-confirmation on the final remediation head (per the round-1 caveat): dependency set differs from r1 (x/net v0.62.0 and x/mod/x/tools/x/sys from the new base; klauspost/compress still dropped). go build ./... (vendored) + go vet pass under go1.27.0; ./pkg/... ./cmd/... build under the exact CI-pinned GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.10; CI unittest/lint/staticcheck green under 1.26.10. Full unit suite at head: 66 ok / 4 FAIL, the same 4 packages fail identically at the new base 91a58c1 (results/unit-suite-base-r2-failures.txt) - environmental, no PR-attributed regression.
